title: Securing Singaporeans' Jobs and Livelihoods, and Foreign Talent Policy
what_it_is: Securing Singaporeans' Jobs and Livelihoods, and Foreign Talent Policy

sections.label: Simultaneous debate question procedure
sections.summary: The House will follow previous simultaneous debate procedures, with questions on both Motions put at the end and amendments that negative the other Motion disallowed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: As the intent of the Business Motion resolved on 13 September 2021 is for the House to follow the procedures of previous simultaneous debates, I will put the questions on both Motions at the end of the debate, so that the House can express its view on each Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: In addition, I will also disallow any amendment to either Motion that has the effect of negativing the other Motion.

sections.label: CECA and PSP stance
sections.summary: The Motion refers to CECA and calls on the Government to address anxiety over foreign talent policy and Movement of Natural Persons provisions in FTAs like CECA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: It specifically refers to CECA and may I remind him of what it says?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I quote, "That this Parliament calls upon the Government to take urgent and concrete action to address the widespread anxiety among Singaporeans on jobs and livelihoods caused by the foreign talent policy and the provisions on Movement of Natural Persons in some free trade agreements like CECA." And this is not something that is thrust upon the PSP or Mr Leong Mun Wai.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I think you will know that, at the launch of the PSP on 3 August 2019, Dr Tan Cheng Bock made it a point to emphasise that PSP was targeting CECA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: And since entering Parliament, Mr Leong, you have repeatedly commented on CECA, comments which carry clear racial undertones.

sections.label: Support for CECA and FTAs
sections.summary: The speaker states that, in general, they are supportive of CECA and FTAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: As for CECA and FTAs, in general, we are supportive.

sections.label: FTA support and MNP concern
sections.summary: They support FTAs in general for trade and investment benefits but are concerned about Movement of Natural Persons provisions in modern FTAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: We are supporting FTAs in general for the benefits that FTAs can bring: trade to our country, investments and all that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: But we are concerned that modern FTAs do have provisions on the Movement of Natural Persons.

sections.label: No full MNP disclosure
sections.summary: The speaker says there is not yet full disclosure on Movement of Natural Persons provisions in CECA and some other FTAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: As I said, in my speech, we do not have full disclosure on the Movement of Natural Persons provisions in CECA yet and, also, some of the other FTAs.

sections.label: Government quoted one year's ICT
sections.summary: The Government quoted only one year's ICT numbers, 500 ICT in 2020, which is a COVID-19 year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The Government only quoted one year's ICT numbers – 500 ICT in 2020, which is a COVID-19 year.

sections.label: Australian FTA dependants, US FTA property
sections.summary: The Australian FTA has a clause letting ICTs bring dependants, and residents gave feedback on US citizens buying property without ABSD.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The Australian FTA also contains a clause allowing ICTs to bring in dependants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: For the US FTA, we have received feedback from residents about why US citizens are allowed to buy properties in Singapore without paying the Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty.

sections.label: CECA immigration control retained
sections.summary: Ong Ye Kung said CECA does not allow free flow of Indians and the Government retains full rights over immigration and foreign manpower.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: My colleague Ong Ye Kung said that CECA does not allow a free flow of Indians into Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He made that very clear to this House and to Mr Leong.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I will also remind Mr Leong that it has been explained that nothing in CECA says that Singapore must unconditionally let PMEs into Singapore, and all foreign PMEs have to meet our work pass conditions in order to come and work here.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Just to remind Members and Mr Leong, I will repeat what Minister Ong had said.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He said in this House, by reference to Chapter 9 of CECA, that it "makes it clear that the Government's ability to regulate immigration and foreign manpower is not affected by the agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Government retains full rights to decide who can enter the country to live, work, become PRs or become citizens.

sections.label: Immigration powers not in question
sections.summary: The speaker says immigration and work pass requirements were never in question in CECA or other FTAs, and cites PSP's claim on 127 professional categories.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Contrary to PSP’s claim, our ability to impose requirements for immigration and work pass has never been in question in CECA or any other FTAs that we have signed." And he made a couple of other points, if I may refer to, "PSP pointed out that CECA listed 127 categories of professionals, hence, claimed that Indian nationals in these professions can all freely come here to work for a year.

sections.label: Disagreement with legal interpretation
sections.summary: The speaker states that as of now, they do not agree to the interpretation of the legal documents as it is now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: As of now, we do not agree to the interpretation of the legal documents as it is now.

sections.label: No legal opinion on provisions
sections.summary: The speaker says that at this point they do not have a legal opinion of those provisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Okay, I can then say that at this point, I do not have a legal opinion of those provisions.

sections.label: ICTs and professionals need work passes
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with Minister Ong that ICTs and the 127 professionals must go through the work pass route.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Minister Ong has pointed out that that is false and that they have to first meet our work pass rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: I agree that all these ICTs and the 127 professionals need to go through our work pass route.

sections.label: Employment Pass and local PMETs
sections.summary: Over the last 10 years, Employment Pass and S Pass holders increased by 110,000 while local PMETs increased by 300,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Over the last 10 years, the last decade, there has been an increase of 110,000 Employment Pass and S Pass holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: During the same period, the local PMETs increased by 300,000.

sections.label: PMET vacancies question
sections.summary: The speaker asks through the Chair about the 30,000 PMET vacancies just mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Can I ask, Sir, through you, I just mentioned there are 30,000 PMET vacancies.

sections.label: Unfilled PMET jobs in July
sections.summary: The number of unfilled PMET jobs was set out in July.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The number of PMET jobs unfilled, that thousands of jobs were being unfilled, was set out in July.

sections.label: Displacement, reskilling, CECA Motion
sections.summary: Displacement is worldwide; the speaker says reskilling and right industries are the way, and rejects racist fervour and a Motion calling CECA terms wrong.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Displacement is taking place all over the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have tried to keep unemployment low, we have tried to create the jobs and many people have gotten jobs and we need to help those who have not got jobs, and the way to do it is to try to reskill them and bring in the right industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: What is not legitimate is to try and create a racist, xenophobic, them-versus-us fervour, put down a Motion saying that the terms of CECA are wrong.

sections.label: Motion on CECA free movement
sections.summary: The Motion says CECA provisions on Movement of Natural Persons allow free movement of Indians, consistent with Leong, PSP and Tan Cheng Bock's statements.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Looking at the Motion, Sir, Mr Leong can fulminate as much as he wants, but it says what it says.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And it says, "the provisions on Movement of Natural Persons in some free trade agreements like CECA", and that is consistent with the position that Mr Leong put forward in July and what he has said in his Facebook post and what PSP has said, that CECA allows free movement of Indians into Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Motion is consistent with what Dr Tan Cheng Bock had said on 3 August 2019, which Minister Ong referenced, and I quote Dr Tan, "amongst the terms of CECA, it allowed the free movement of professionals in 127 sectors to enter and work in Singapore." Mr Leong has confirmed that that is not accurate, because he says it is subject to our work pass rules, but this was what they were thinking.

sections.label: No legal opinion on agreement
sections.summary: The speaker says that at this point they have no legal opinion on the provisions under the agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Okay, Sir, as I have said just now, at this point, I do not have any legal opinion on the provisions provided under the agreement.

sections.label: CECA terms and Leong's view
sections.summary: Speaker asks whether agreed CECA terms are in black and white and says Mr Leong has no view on whether they harm Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: So, for those specific parts of the agreement, do you agree that those are in black and white, what was agreed?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, through you, Sir, therefore I can confirm that if Mr Leong has no opinion, then naturally, he has no view as to whether the terms of CECA are negative for Singapore.

sections.label: Leong's changed beliefs
sections.summary: Speaker asks whether Mr Leong still holds those beliefs or has changed his mind, and states he appears to have changed it.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I am asking whether he continues to have those beliefs or has he changed his mind.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Therefore, Mr Leong has changed his mind, it appears, Sir, from last year.

sections.label: Leong quote on DBS CEO
sections.summary: Speaker quotes Mr Leong saying he is deeply disappointed that 22 years after Mr Wong's 1998 appointment DBS still lacks a homegrown CEO.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I will just, for the record, set out exactly what was said by Mr Leong.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He said and I quote: "I am deeply disappointed now ...", that these are the points that he was speaking, "...because 22 years later after Mr –" and I assume after Mr Wong's appointment in 1998, "...DBS is still without a homegrown CEO".

sections.label: Welcoming committed talent, rejecting baiting
sections.summary: Speaker says welcoming talent who take up citizenship is not wrong, but targeting new citizens and PRs from specific countries is race-baiting and nationality-baiting.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I would say, Sir, to this House, it is not wrong that we welcome talent when people are committed enough to take up citizenship.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is wrong to have an issue with new citizens and PRs from specific countries because it is quite clear what Mr Leong and PSP were doing.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is race-baiting and nationality-baiting without beating about the bush.

sections.label: Local PMET job figures
sections.summary: Speaker asks whether locals are being pushed out of PMET jobs, citing over 300,000 local PMET jobs created and locals holding 80% of them.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Is it that locals are being pushed out of PMET jobs on a large scale?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have created over 300,000 local PMET jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In fact, locals take up 80% of all PMET jobs.

sections.label: FTAs, CECA and work passes
sections.summary: Speaker accepts FTAs created jobs, notes CECA does not give Indian nationals free rein, but asks whether work pass regulation has failed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, we accept that FTAs have encouraged investments and created jobs and opportunities for both Singaporeans as well as foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, we note the Government's explanation that CECA does not allow Indian nationals free rein to enter Singapore and that the entry of foreigners who seek employment is regulated by the Government and, specifically, MOM's work pass policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, we believe that it is fair to ask whether the Government and MOM, for many years past, have failed to regulate work passes in the best way possible.

sections.label: Workers' Party on job creation
sections.summary: The Workers' Party does not assume pro-trade policies and FTAs like CECA automatically create good jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Third, the Workers' Party does not assume that good jobs are automatically created for Singaporeans by virtue of Singapore's pro-trade policies and a strong network of FTAs, including CECA.

sections.label: Call for aggressive government intervention
sections.summary: The view is that the Government must intervene aggressively through policy or legislation and ensure stronger safety nets for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Our view is that the Government needs to intervene aggressively through policy or legislation to ameliorate this and ensure the availability of stronger safety nets for Singaporeans who cannot make the transition.

sections.label: Five proposals on jobs and foreign employment
sections.summary: Five proposals: track skills transfers, consider fixed-term EPs, track underemployment, set up a Select Committee, and communicate better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One, policies and procedures must be introduced to more effectively promote and track skills transfers from foreigners to Singaporeans; two, fixed-term EPs tied to skills transfers should be considered; three, the problem of underemployment must be tracked and solved; four, the Government should consider setting up a Parliamentary Standing Select Committee dedicated to overseeing this issue of jobs and foreign employment; and five, the Government needs to communicate more and much better on jobs and foreign employment that it has been doing up to now.

sections.label: Capability Transfer Programme and skills transfer KPI
sections.summary: The CTP spent $5 million over five years benefiting 970 Singaporeans; skills transfer should be publicly tracked as a KPI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I spoke about the Capability Transfer Programme (CTP) during the Committee of Supply debates this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This Government programme has been extended to 2024 and, in its own words, seeks to, I quote, “support pervasive innovation throughout the economy and build deep capabilities in our local workforce to support companies, associations and professional bodies to speed up the transfer of global capabilities into Singapore”, unquote.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In response to my queries in Parliament, the Government reported that $5 million has been spent over the last five years and this initiative has benefited 970 Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I note that the CTP is only one arrow in the Government’s quiver, but this only reiterates the point that a holistic assessment and reporting of the transfer of skills from foreigners to Singaporeans is necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I suggest that the extent of skills transfer from foreigners to locals be publicly tracked, monitored and reported as a Key Performance Indicator, or KPI, for each sector in the revised Industry Transformation Roadmaps under ITM 2.0.

sections.label: Fixed-term Employment Pass renewal condition
sections.summary: A fixed-term EP would be renewed only if the company proves Singaporean workers benefited from skills upgrading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A fixed-term EP would be one that would only be renewed if the applicant company can prove that, under the previous EP, Singaporean workers in the company or in the industry have benefited from skills upgrading.

sections.label: MOM on underemployment definitions
sections.summary: MOM said time-related underemployment is the only internationally accepted definition, and no internationally recognised way exists to track skill-related underemployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MOM said at the time that time-related underemployment is the only internationally accepted statistical definition of underemployment and since it is recommended by the International Labour Organization or ILO, Singapore follows that norm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim spoke again on underemployment in her 2019 Budget debate speech, to which the former Minister for Manpower responded that MOM is interested in tracking other forms of underemployment, such as skill-related underemployment, but reiterated that there were no internationally recognised ways of doing so.

sections.label: Workers' Party jobs suggestions
sections.summary: The Workers' Party suggests publicly tracking underemployment and a permanent Parliamentary Standing Select Committee on jobs and foreign employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers’ Party suggests that there is an urgent need to publicly track underemployment amongst Singaporeans and to publish such findings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My fourth suggestion is that there should be a check and balance of a dedicated platform where the policy-makers can be questioned, and this is the suggestion of a permanent Parliamentary Standing Select Committee dedicated to the issue of jobs and foreign employment.

sections.label: Ministry foreign manpower data
sections.summary: The Ministry does not disclose foreign manpower data broken down by nationality, including data on ICTs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Ministry does not disclose data on foreign manpower with breakdown by nationality, including data on ICTs.” Unquote.

sections.label: Tan See Leng ICT figure
sections.summary: Minister Tan See Leng revealed that the number of ICTs from India was 500 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Minister Tan See Leng revealed that the number of ICTs from India was a low figure of 500 in the year 2020.

sections.label: Question on ICTs from India
sections.summary: A call is made for the Government to answer Mr Leon Perera's 2016 question on ICTs from India under CECA from 2005 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To help us base today’s debate on facts, may I call on the Government to now answer the question asked by Mr Leon Perera in 2016: how many ICTs have come from India under CECA from 2005 to 2019?

sections.label: CECA benefited 97,000 Singaporeans
sections.summary: One prominent figure in the digital notices is that 97,000 Singaporeans have benefited from CECA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One prominent figure in the digital notices is that 97,000 Singaporeans have benefited from CECA.

sections.label: Select Committee online falsehoods traits
sections.summary: In 2018, the Select Committee for Deliberate Online Falsehoods identified traits in social media ecology such as confirmation bias, the illusory truth effect, and the slow drip of falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2018, the report of the Select Committee for Deliberate Online Falsehoods identified particular traits within the ecology of social media, such as confirmation bias, the illusory truth effect, and the slow drip of falsehoods.

sections.label: Racial balance and foreign workers
sections.summary: The speaker suggests bad actors could exploit Singapore's racial balance amid US-China tensions, and urges clarifying job data to address Singaporeans' concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the face of a US-China Cold War and our majority ethnic Chinese population, I would suggest that it is perfectly within the contemplation of other bad actors to use Singapore's racial balance to play out one act of a modern great game amongst our local population, pitting Indians against Chinese as an overlay to fraught Sino-Indian relations and to build up more anger against Indian workers and India in general.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There is some data out there on jobs, which the Government releases every now and then.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If we can clarify issues that disturb Singaporeans who would inevitably have less information than the Government, we would be able to focus singularly on the progress being made by the Singaporean PMETs and workers, and address gaps that develop.

sections.label: Foreigners, economy and investor confidence
sections.summary: The passage states Singaporeans count foreigners as friends, workers feel excluded, and Minister Lawrence Wong said debate tone matters for investor confidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Many Singaporeans count the foreigners in our midst, regardless of race, language or religion, as our friends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But it is precisely because we need foreigners to power our economy that we need to pay more attention to Singapore workers, some of whom feel excluded from opportunities created in their homeland." The Minister for Finance Lawrence Wong, in reference to the Ministerial Statement made by Minister Ong Ye Kung and Minister Tan See Leng, said that the tone of how we debate the issue matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister said that if investors start to feel that Singapore is less hospitable to foreign investment and talent, they will surely look for other options and there are many compelling options everywhere in the world.

sections.label: Workers' Party amendment to Motion
sections.summary: The Workers' Party says Singaporean workers' and PMETs' anxieties are real and proposes an amendment to the Minister for Finance's Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The anxieties and concerns of the Singaporean worker and PMET are real.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Our workers carry the same fears and concerns for their children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is for this reason that the Workers’ Party proposes an amendment to the Minister for Finance's Motion, which I seek to share with this House.

sections.label: Wording changes and proactive disclosure
sections.summary: The passage explains replacing 'supports' with 'calls on stronger' and adding limb (f) for proactive disclosure to counter misinformation and encourage fact-based conversation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The inclusion of the words "calls on stronger" in place of "supports", reinforces the importance of correcting course and adjusting or changing policies going forward to address the anxieties amongst Singaporeans that limb (a) of the Minister's Motion acknowledges has taken root in the recent past.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The new limb (f) captures what we in the Workers' Party believe represents a fundamental change of culture needed with respect to information disclosure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: A proactive approach to disclosure would operate to take the sting out of misinformation campaigns that ride on job and unemployment insecurity, and encourage a fact-based conversation amongst our people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: This would, in turn, buttress efforts amongst Singaporeans to provide feedback on gaps and solutions that can improve outcomes for the Singaporean worker and PMET.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: This limb is not inconsistent with the Government's acknowledgement in July that it is better for data, for example, such as that requested by Leon Perera on ICT numbers, and this is my example, to come out early when it concerns issues like racism or xenophobia and that it is much better to quell these issues earlier.

sections.label: New limb (f) and EP numbers
sections.summary: The passage inserts limb (f) on releasing jobs, Free Trade Agreements and foreign worker policy information, and cites rising EP holders from India.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: At (e), to include the word "and" at the end of the sentence after the semi-colon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: And to insert a whole new limb (f), which reads, "calls on the Government to proactively release information on jobs and employment prospects of Singaporeans and the costs and benefits of Free Trade Agreements and foreign worker policies with a view to formulating better policies to ensure Singaporeans secure good jobs in Singapore and are not disadvantaged when seeking employment." Ms Hazel Poa.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Minister for Manpower has revealed that the proportion of EP holders from India has increased from one in seven in 2005, to a quarter in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Based on 65,000 EP holders in 2005 and 177,000 EP holders in 2020, we can calculate that the number of EP holders from India increased by 377% from 2005 to 2020, an average growth rate of 11% per year.

sections.label: Growth outstrips global trend
sections.summary: The passage states that the 377% growth in Singapore far outstrips the global trend.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The growth of 377% in Singapore far outstrips the global trend.

sections.label: Work Permit and S Pass quotas
sections.summary: Quotas apply to Work Permits and S Passes, while Employment Passes have no quota and require minimum salaries of $4,500, or $5,000 in finance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Currently, quotas are imposed on Work Permits and S Passes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There is no quota for Employment Passes which are for jobs with a minimum salary of $4,500 and, in the case of the finance industry, $5,000.

sections.label: Local PME jobs increase
sections.summary: The Minister said local PME jobs increased by 380,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Minister has said that local PME jobs have increased by 380,000.

sections.label: Reclassification in PME job figures
sections.summary: The speaker asks MOM whether the 380,000 local PME job increase includes job holders' status changes, and how many new jobs remain after netting off reclassification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While not all the 300,000 increase in citizens and PRs are holding PME jobs, it still suggests that a significant portion of the 380,000 increase in local PME jobs could have come from a change in the status of the job holders and not due to the creation of new jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Can MOM clarify whether the changes arising from the change in the status of the job holder is included in the 380,000?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If so, how many new local PME jobs were created after netting off the effect of reclassification?

sections.label: Measuring underemployment in Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether attempts were made to measure underemployment and, if so, for information on its extent and trend over 20 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Given that this concern has been raised for many years, have we made any attempts to measure underemployment?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If so, can MOM share the information on the extent and trend of underemployment in Singapore in the last 20 years?

sections.label: Migrant labour and real wage growth
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry has studied how labour force growth depresses real wage growth and, if so, its conclusion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Increasing labour supply by bringing in migrant workers increases economic growth but dampens local wages, a trend that we observed in our study using statistics from 2009 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: We would like to ask the Minister for Manpower whether the Ministry has studied the effects of how labour force growth depresses real wage growth and, if so, what is their conclusion.

sections.label: Foreign manpower proportion target
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the one-third foreign manpower target still holds and whether the Government turns down FDIs requiring a higher proportion of foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: The Government had previously indicated that it is aiming to limit the proportion of foreign manpower in our labour force to one third.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Is that still the target this Government is holding to?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: With this target in mind, does the Government turn down FDIs that would require a higher proportion of foreigners?

sections.label: Licensed HR managers for employers
sections.summary: Large employers should be required to hire licensed human resource managers personally responsible for compliance with manpower regulations, with penalties including licence loss.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Large employers should be required to hire licensed human resource managers who will have personal responsibilities to ensure full compliance with Government manpower regulations and, those who do not, risk penalties, which can include losing their licence.

sections.label: Reducing reliance on foreign manpower
sections.summary: It asks when reliance on foreign manpower becomes an overdose and calls for reducing it, watching wage growth, and pegging ministerial salaries to the median wage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: At what point does it become an overdose?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: We are not asking for a closed economy or a closed labour market but a reduction in our reliance on foreign manpower to a lower level and keeping a close eye on wage growth while we adjust the level of foreign participation in our labour force.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: It would also be a good time to reiterate that Ministerial Salaries should be pegged to the median wage.

sections.label: Singaporean worker percentage as KPI
sections.summary: The percentage of Singaporean workers should be made a Government key performance indicator.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Make the percentage of Singaporean workers into a Government key performance indicator (KPI).

sections.label: CECA quotes and objections
sections.summary: It cites Lee Hsien Loong and George Yeo on CECA, asks if CECA is being misrepresented, and objects to implications that free trade discussions stir racism.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: On 29 June 2005, at the dinner after the signing of CECA, Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said, "As economic linkages expand and a free flow of people and ideas continues, I am confident that the relationship will grow from strength to strength." Mr George Yeo, on 2 March 2006, during the Committee of Supply, said, "Professionals like doctors, accountants and engineers are able to move back and forth freely, operating within the same legal and regulatory framework." Does this imply that they are also making attempts to misrepresent CECA?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: This focus on semantics and technicalities instead of the underlying causes is rather disappointing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: We also object to the implication that discussions on free trade agreements stir up racism and xenophobia.

sections.label: Raising EP and S Pass salaries
sections.summary: He had suggested raising EP qualifying salaries from $4,500 to $10,000 and S Passes from $2,500 to $4,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: First, in relation to work passes, he had suggested that we raise the EP qualifying salaries from the current $4,500 to $10,000, and for S Passes to be raised from $2,500 to $4,500.

sections.label: Leong on PRs and work passes
sections.summary: Mr Leong attributed the 80,000 PRs given at the height of immigration all to work pass holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Third, Mr Leong attributed the 80,000 PRs given at the height of immigration all to work pass holders.

sections.label: Factors in real wage growth
sections.summary: Real average wage growth at the overall economy level depends on labour productivity growth, growth in labour's terms of trade and growth in the labour share of output.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Real average wage growth at the overall economy level depends on three factors, namely, labour productivity growth, growth in labour's terms of trade and growth in the labour share of output.

sections.label: NTUC-SNEF PME taskforce engagements
sections.summary: Through NTUC-SNEF PME taskforce engagements, ground sentiments on issues and challenges faced by Singaporean PMEs were heard from more than 9,000 of them in the past eight months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Through the NTUC-SNEF PME taskforce engagements, we have heard ground sentiments on a plethora of issues and challenges faced by Singaporean PMEs, more than 9,000 of them, all Singaporeans, in the past eight months.

sections.label: Anecdotes of EP holders employed
sections.summary: Anecdotes from PMEs about EP holders employed for jobs Singaporeans can take on are a minority, confined to certain sectors and companies, and not widespread.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Fortunately, anecdotes from PMEs who shared how they have encountered instances of EP holders being employed for jobs that Singaporeans can take on are a minority and confined to certain sectors and companies, and not widespread.

sections.label: Motion by Leong Mun Wai rejected
sections.summary: The speaker cannot accept the Motion standing in the name of Non-Constituency Member Mr Leong Mun Wai, and welcomes the Tripartite Committee on Workplace Fairness and fair employment guidelines becoming law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: On this note and for these very facts and circumstances, I, therefore, cannot accept the Motion standing in the name of Non-Constituency Member Mr Leong Mun Wai.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Government has responded to our advocacy efforts and calls with the setting up of the Tripartite Committee on Workplace Fairness, and Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong in his National Day Rally addressed and updated that we will look at fair employment guidelines becoming law and the set-up of a new tribunal to address workplace discrimination by those few black sheep.

sections.label: NTUC role in workplace fairness
sections.summary: NTUC will represent workers and PMEs and contribute actively in the Tripartite Committee on Workplace Fairness to improve workplace fairness through legislative and non-legislative options and tackle workplace discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: NTUC will represent the voices of our workers and PMEs, and contribute actively in the Tripartite Committee on Workplace Fairness (TCWF) to look into improving workplace fairness through both legislative and non-legislative options and consider measures to tackle workplace discrimination.

sections.label: HR certification and Singaporean Core
sections.summary: It is important to increase certification and accreditation of HR practitioners and provide shared HR services for SMEs, and recommendations to strengthen the Singaporean Core will continue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: It is, therefore, important we move towards increasing certification and accreditation of HR practitioners, as well as providing shared HR services for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: We will also continue to surface recommendations to strengthen the Singaporean Core and this will include: first, enhancing the EP application review process by considering a range of factors beyond the individual applicant’s education, qualification and salary; second, facilitating skills transfer from foreign specialists to local PMEs through skills transfer programmes.

sections.label: Worker protection and skills upgrading
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Motion by Minister Lawrence Wong on managing manpower, fair treatment of workers and skills upgrading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In the same vein, we need to see that they are adequately protected, have access to quality jobs and are equipped with the relevant skills to prepare for the future economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I, therefore, support the Motion by Minister Lawrence Wong which acknowledges Singaporeans' anxieties and for the Government to take action to manage the population of manpower, ensuring fair treatment of workers by employers and investing in skills upgrading.

sections.label: Population White Paper debate 2013
sections.summary: In 2013, then Deputy Prime Minister Teo said growth in foreign workforce, population, infrastructure and housing were not aligned and caused anxiety.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In 2013, during the debate around our Population White Paper with the now "iconic" 6.9 million figure, then Deputy Prime Minister Teo told this House that “the growth in foreign workforce, total population, infrastructure and housing are not aligned", and accepted that it "contributed to the anxiety, crowdedness, integration problems and the daily inconveniences faced by Singaporeans today".

sections.label: Globalisation, foreign labour reliance
sections.summary: Globalisation has slowed since 2010 and reliance on foreign labour may be an Achilles heel if workers cannot always come.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Movement of people, goods and services, has become much easier, and, together with the growth in the middle classes in massive and emerging economies, such as China and India, has had an impact on our domestic markets and society in general.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But it must not be forgotten that globalisation has slowed down since 2010 and the trend of increasing globalisation is not a linear process, as history has, indeed, taught us.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Our reliance on foreign labour, whether skilled labour or the low-wage migrants we see taking up the slack as carers in our medical and social systems, as live-in help for households, and also for building sites, may prove to be our Achilles heel if we assume that we can simply turn on the tap for these roles to be fulfilled at any time, and that the workers will come in.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Our policies, including our FTAs, need to be sensitive to this and not be blind-sided by any reverses in globalisation trends which are currently threatening to be the case.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is especially important in the current era, where we see the rise of nativist politics and governments from around 2016, as evidenced most famously by the Brexit vote and election of Donald Trump.

sections.label: Bridges and data-driven culture
sections.summary: Two areas to work on are building bridges between immigrants and citizens and embracing a transparent, data-driven culture.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Two big areas where we can work on more are: first, building more, stronger and meaningful bridges between immigrants and citizens; and second, embracing a strong, transparent and data-driven culture.

sections.label: Integration as two-way process
sections.summary: The European Programme for Integration and Migration calls integration a two-way process, and it is unclear how successful People's Association initiatives have been.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To this end, it is notable that the European Programme for Integration and Migration states that this is, quote, "a two-way process of adaption by migrants and host societies, and, of identification and respect for a core set of values that bind migrants and host communities in a common purpose", unquote.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While I note that there are initiatives organised through the People’s Association, what has been less clear to the public is whether the organisation itself is seen to be there primarily to serve partisan interests and, more importantly, how successful these initiatives have been.

sections.label: Ground-up interaction and rights protection
sections.summary: The speaker wants more ground-up avenues for citizen-immigrant interaction, a no-excuses approach to discrimination, and notes ICA and MOM give no reasons for decisions.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I only wish that we see more of these, and that we continually look for ways and means to improve the situation, to allow more ground-up, non-Government-directed avenues for interaction and understanding between citizens and immigrants, allowing voices to be heard from both sides.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That said, we also need to have a no-excuses approach to discriminatory, prejudicial behaviour and against those who seek to sow discord between immigrants and our host communities.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Both groups deserve to have their rights protected stringently.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: At the moment, decisions on whether or not to grant citizenship, permanent residence and various work passes are made by ICA and MOM respectively, but no reasons are ever given.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Likewise, data relating to our resident labour force often lumps Singaporeans and Permanent Residents together.

sections.label: Government sharing workforce and citizenship data
sections.summary: The Government should proactively publish data on workforce, citizenship pathways and hot-button topics so citizens and academics understand policy impact.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Government thus needs to take the lead in this by being proactive about the type of data that is shared: from information about our workforce broken down into Singaporeans and Permanent Residents, to providing clear pathways to citizenship for those who are already part of our Singaporean families and communities.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Data on these hot-button topics should be published and shared regularly to allow citizens to understand the impact of Government-led policies on the shape of our economy and society and to allow our academics and commentators a fact base to start with.

sections.label: Anti-discrimination legislation in Parliament
sections.summary: The passage states that anti-discrimination legislation in Parliament is a right move.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In this respect, anti-discrimination legislation in Parliament is a right move.

sections.label: Proposed amendment to Motion rejected
sections.summary: The Member's proposed amendment deleting words on Movement of Natural Persons and replacing them is judged not relevant and substantively changes the Motion's tone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Member has moved to propose the amendment as follows: To delete the words "and the provisions on Movement of Natural Persons in some free trade agreements like the Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement".

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: And replace them with a similar paragraph as what they have proposed earlier to the other Motion, which is "by proactively releasing information on jobs and employment prospects of Singaporeans and the costs and benefits of free trade agreements and foreign worker policies, with a view to formulating better policies to ensure Singaporeans secure good jobs in Singapore and are not disadvantaged when seeking employment." I am of the view that the last paragraph is similar to what you have proposed in a previous Motion and we should confine that to that Motion so that Members can vote accordingly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Your proposal to delete the words "and the provisions on Movement of Natural Persons in some free trade agreements like the Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement" substantively changes the tone of what that Motion was about in the first place, which is being debated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: So, in my view, the proposed amendments would not be relevant.

sections.label: Reviewing FTAs and foreign work passes
sections.summary: The passage welcomes continued control over foreign work passes and echoes calls to regularly study FTAs' net economic benefit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, we have little to give away unless we open up our services sectors or our labour market further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Government has clarified that it maintains an intent to continue maintaining close control over the granting of foreign work passes without any FTA provision diluting that and this is a commitment that this House will, I am sure, hold this Government and future governments to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Because FTAs are a negotiated compromise, at any one point in time, it is necessary to review these agreements from time to time to ensure that what we have given away is not proved too much and what we are getting back is as good as what we expected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Therefore, I echo the calls made by the Leader of the Opposition and my colleague, Member of Parliament for Sengkang, Ms He Ting Ru, to regularly study the impact of our FTAs, to engage research to quantify the net economic benefit over costs.

sections.label: Assessing FTA utilisation rates
sections.summary: The Government should regularly assess local FTA utilisation rates and perceived benefits, and publish SME utilisation rates for public debate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Moreover, the Government should regularly assess local FTA utilisation rates and perceived benefits to see if the other country is delivering on its market access commitments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: FTA utilisation rates by SMEs should be published to help all stakeholders assess our efforts in public debate.

sections.label: Fixed-term employment passes for transferability
sections.summary: Fixed-term EPs would be granted for a fixed term, localised, and not renewed by default unless employers show extenuating circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One antidote to the transferability deficit is fixed-term EPs, the suggestion I made in this House previously in which the Leader of the Opposition alluded to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These would be foreign work passes granted for a fixed term with the understanding that the job has to be localised in that term and the pass, as a default, would not be renewed, unless the employer can demonstrate strong extenuating circumstances to appeal for a renewal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Fixed-term work passes should be one tool in our toolkit not just to advance transferability of foreigners' skills towards locals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are other tools that can be used to advance transferability that Workers' Party Members of Parliament in this House have argued for, such as stimulating cross-border remote working internships for our students and young adults with cutting-edge multinational corporations abroad which were not present in Singapore, for example.

sections.label: Foreigner population burdens scarce resources
sections.summary: A large foreigner population to create jobs burdens land, healthcare, roads and public transport, and risks work cultures disadvantaging Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A large population of foreigners to create jobs for Singaporeans places burdens on our scarce resources of land, healthcare capacity, road capacity, public transport and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It also runs the risk of entrenching work cultures that disadvantage Singaporeans in the longer term, especially if the foreigners start off from a higher skills base in a new industry.

sections.label: Tie FDI incentives to employment passes
sections.summary: It proposes tying foreign direct investment incentives to fixed-term employment passes and expanding local university places for future industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Thirdly, tie foreign direct investment incentives to a number of fixed-term EPs to ensure Singaporeans' pathway into new industries, as discussed earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Fourthly, can we examine if we need to expand University education places for locals in disciplines necessary for future industries, thus managing the need to import foreign manpower with degrees from, in some cases, less highly ranked universities than our local ones?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This ties to another Workers' Party manifesto point on expanding University capacity to 50% of the cohort size.

sections.label: Reconciling views on trades jobs
sections.summary: It asks how to reconcile two contradictory perspectives and address why SME owners say Singaporeans avoid trades jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How do we reconcile these two different and seemingly contradictory perspectives?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We need to deeply address the reasons why SME business owners say Singaporeans do not want to take up trades jobs.

sections.label: Productivity conditions and phasing out
sections.summary: It suggests harder productivity conditions for Government contracts and clear long-term timelines for phasing out low productivity work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, can we introduce harder productivity conditions for Government contracts?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And there should be clear long-term timelines for phasing out low productivity work, not ad hoc short-term changes to foreign manpower quotas done in an unpredictable fashion.

sections.label: Foreign tradespersons citizenship and underemployment
sections.summary: It proposes pathways for foreign tradespersons to become citizens to supplement locals, and measuring underemployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Fifthly, we need to create pathways for some good trades persons who are foreigners to become citizens in small enough numbers, not to suppress but to supplement locals moving into these sectors, and then nudge those new citizens to transfer skills to more locals in the ways we have spoken about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Are such trades persons given the opportunity to become citizens now even if they have no university degree?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And sixth – and this is another call the Workers' Party has made and the Leader of the Opposition has alluded to – we need to measure underemployment so that we can tackle it.

sections.label: ICT numbers in 2020
sections.summary: The total number of ICTs in 2020 was 4,200, and the total number of Indian ICTs was 500.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The total number of ICTs in 2020 was 4,200.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The total number of Indian ICTs in 2020 was 500.

sections.label: Data location reply to Poa
sections.summary: The speaker told Ms Hazel Poa where to find the data and that it goes back to 1991 on MOM's website.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, in my reply to Ms Hazel Poa, I told her where to look for such data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: I also told her that the data stretches back to 1991 on the MOM's website, if she was interested.

sections.label: Opposing PSP Motion on anxieties
sections.summary: The speaker acknowledges anxieties about jobs and competition but opposes the PSP's Motion as it lacks the solutions Singaporeans seek.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: I acknowledge these anxieties – they are present, but they are not just present in Singapore alone.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: I oppose the PSP’s Motion because it does not provide the solutions that Singaporeans anxious about jobs and competition seek.

sections.label: EP, S Pass and local PMET growth
sections.summary: Over the past decade EP and S Pass holders rose 110,000 while local PMETs rose 300,000, and in sub-sectors 40,000 versus almost 155,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Over the past decade, there was an increase of 110,000 Employment Pass (EP) and S Pass holders, but local PMETs increased by 300,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Over the past decade, EP and S Pass holders in these sub-sectors increased by 40,000, but local PMETs increased by almost 155,000 – almost four times.

sections.label: Local PME growth to Singaporeans
sections.summary: In the 6 July Ministerial Statement the speaker shared that most local PME growth over the last decade went to Singaporeans born in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: During the 6 July Ministerial Statement, I have already shared that the majority of local PME growth over the last decade went to Singaporeans born in Singapore.

sections.label: Unfilled PMET jobs by sector
sections.summary: The trend has risen since 2010 and hovered around 30,000 over five years, with 4,300 unfilled PMET jobs in Infocomm, 4,100 in Finance and 2,700 in Professional Services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: It has been on an upward trend since 2010 and has been hovering around 30,000 over the past five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: There are 4,300 unfilled PMET jobs in Infocomm, 4,100 unfilled PMET jobs in Finance, 2,700 unfilled PMET jobs in Professional Services.

sections.label: Summary of PMET data table
sections.summary: The data, put in a table, shows foreign PMETs increased but local PMET employment, job vacancies and wages grew while local PMET unemployment stayed low.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: To sum up, looking at the data, and I have put it in a table for everyone to see, the data shows us that while the number of foreign PMETs has increased, we saw: one, an even larger increase in local PMET employment; two, low local PMET unemployment; three, a growing number of PMET job vacancies; and four, growing local PMET wages.

sections.label: Resident time-related underemployment rate
sections.summary: The resident time-related underemployment rate averaged 3.6% over the past 10 years and rose to 4.1% in 2020 due to COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The resident time-related underemployment rate has averaged 3.6% over the past 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Although the resident time-related underemployment rate rose to 4.1% in 2020 due to COVID-19, it still remains relatively low.

sections.label: Proportion of SEPs
sections.summary: The proportion of SEPs stayed between 8% and 10% over the past two decades, with an uptick during COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The proportion of SEPs has remained stable at between 8% and 10% over the past two decades, although we did see an uptick during COVID-19.

sections.label: Local workforce in occupation
sections.summary: Around 1.5% of the local workforce works in this particular occupation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Around 1.5% of our local workforce is working in this particular occupation.

sections.label: MNCs creating local PMET jobs
sections.summary: The 10 biggest MNCs in Singapore alone create around 30,000 local PMET jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The 10 biggest MNCs in Singapore alone create around 30,000 local PMET jobs.

sections.label: Requests on work pass rules
sections.summary: They cited unfair wage competition from no CPF for foreigners and asked for higher qualifying salaries, an EP levy, and work pass and nationality caps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: They said that there is an unfair wage competition because employers do not have to pay the 17% CPF contribution for foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: They have asked us to raise the EP qualifying salary to $10,000 and the S Pass qualifying salary to $4,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: They have asked us to impose a $1,200 EP levy, to impose a 25% to 30% cap on work pass holders and PRs and to impose a hard nationality cap of 10% in each firm.

sections.label: EP qualifying salary for 40s
sections.summary: The EP qualifying salary for those in their 40s is around double the minimum qualifying salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: For example, the EP qualifying salary for those in their 40s is around double the minimum qualifying salary.

sections.label: False declaration penalties under EFMA
sections.summary: False declarations are an offence under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act, punishable by a fine up to $20,000, up to two years' imprisonment, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: False declarations of any sorts are an offence under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act (EFMA).

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: It carries a fine of up to $20,000, up to two years' imprisonment or both.

sections.label: Levy on EP holders
sections.summary: The passage states a proposal to impose a levy of $1,200 on all EP holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Second, imposing, a levy of $1,200 on all EP holders.

sections.label: Work pass and PR cap
sections.summary: The passage states a proposal for a 25% to 30% cap on work pass holders and Permanent Residents, and notes existing S Pass quotas and a reduced S Pass Sub-Dependency Ratio Ceiling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Third, imposing a 25% to 30% cap on work pass holders and Permanent Residents in the long run.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: First, I think PSP should know that we have quotas at the S Pass level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We have already been reducing the S Pass Sub-Dependency Ratio Ceiling over the past decade for the services sector.

sections.label: Singaporeans in project financing team
sections.summary: In 2003, Singaporeans made up 40% of its project financing team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: In 2003, Singaporeans accounted for 40% of its project financing team.

sections.label: FCF watchlist single nationality
sections.summary: The Fair Consideration Framework watchlist identifies firms with a high concentration of a single nationality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) watchlist identifies firms with high concentration of a single nationality.

sections.label: Tripartite fair employment guidelines
sections.summary: Tripartite partners issued fair employment guidelines over two decades, including non-discriminatory job advertisement guidelines in 1999, and set up TAFEP in 2006.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: In fact, the tripartite partners have been issuing guidelines on fair employment practices over the past two decades, having introduced the tripartite guidelines on non-discriminatory job advertisements as early as 1999.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: In 2006, we set up the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP).

sections.label: FCF job advertising requirement
sections.summary: The 2014 introduction of the FCF added the job advertising requirement, and the FCF has been progressively strengthened since.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: In 2014, the introduction of the FCF took these efforts one step further by introducing the job advertising requirement and we have been progressively strengthening the FCF ever since.

sections.label: FCF coverage and discrimination legislation
sections.summary: The FCF job advertising requirement was extended to S Passes and the minimum advertising period doubled from 14 to 28 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: In the same year, we extended the coverage of the FCF job advertising requirement to S Passes and doubled the minimum job advertising period from 14 to 28 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: At the National Day Rally 2021 recently, Prime Minister Lee announced we are taking the next step of strengthening our enforcement against workplace discrimination through legislation.

sections.label: Protections for platform workers
sections.summary: An Advisory Committee was established to explore strengthening protections for SEPs working for online platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Government is paying closer attention to SEPs working for online platforms because they have an employee-like relationship with these platforms, but they are not covered under the Employment Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We have established an Advisory Committee to explore how to strengthen protections for these platform workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We will continue to provide training and job-matching services for other SEPs who wish to transit into regular employment.

sections.label: Local employment and FTAs
sections.summary: Local employment has increased as a result of FTAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: In July and now, we have shown you that local employment has increased as a result of FTAs.

sections.label: Motion by Minister Lawrence Wong
sections.summary: The Motion acknowledges anxieties, affirms achievements, preserves what worked and points out work to be done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Motion put forward by Minister Lawrence Wong acknowledges our anxieties, while affirming our achievements; preserves what has worked well, while pointing out the work to be done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: And I repeat what Minister Ong Ye Kung and Minister Lawrence Wong have said: we are prepared to fight the next General Election on these principles.

sections.label: Figures for locals and EPs
sections.summary: On 6 July the numbers were 380,000 locals and 112,000 EPs, and today 300 and 100.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: On 6 July, your number was 380,000 for locals and 112,000 for EPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Today, you give us a figure of 300 and 100.

sections.label: PME and EP statistics timeframe
sections.summary: The speaker says the statistics quoted cover 10 years, from 2010 to 2020, and distinguishes PMETs from PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: On 6 July, it is 15 years from 2005 to 2020 and, at that time, we were talking about PMEs and EPs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: When we have time, I can actually segregate and explain to you the difference between PMETs, which are the equivalent of the EPs and S Passes; and PMEs, which are just the equivalent of the EPs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, today, the statistics quoted to you are for 10 years, from 2010 to 2020.

sections.label: Local PME growth to Singaporeans
sections.summary: The majority of local PME growth over the last 10 years went to Singaporeans born in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The majority of the local PME growth over the last 10 years went to Singaporeans born in Singapore – the majority.

sections.label: Majority PME growth, unemployment data
sections.summary: The speaker repeats that the majority of local PME growth went to Singaporeans born in Singapore, meaning more than 50%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: During the 6 July Ministerial Statement, I had already shared that the majority of local PME growth over the last decade went to Singaporeans born in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I know you want a specific percentage, it is a majority, so, it is more than 50%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Some of the other data points we have published should make it clear that Singaporeans have benefited.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We regularly publish unemployment rates for PRs and citizens.

sections.label: Jobs to local-born Singaporeans
sections.summary: The speaker states that the majority of the jobs went to local bred and born Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Ms Poa, I have said that the majority of the jobs went to local bred and born Singaporeans.

sections.label: Jobs to Singaporeans, CECA opposition
sections.summary: The speaker says the majority of jobs created went to Singaporeans and opposes the Motion's statement that free trade agreements like CECA cause job anxieties.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I am very mindful of and I am actually trying to understand the Member's question here.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But the majority of the jobs created went to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I also oppose the Motion proposed by Mr Leong Mun Wai to the extent that it states free trade agreements like CECA are responsible for the anxieties created for Singaporeans in relation to jobs.

sections.label: Fair Consideration Framework requirement
sections.summary: Companies must comply with the Fair Consideration Framework, giving consideration to the resident population before applying for foreign work passes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Currently, companies are required to actually comply with the Fair Consideration Framework, which means that they must give consideration to the resident population first before they apply for foreign work passes.

sections.label: CECA free trade agreement
sections.summary: CECA is primarily a free trade agreement allowing goods and services to flow freely between India and Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, CECA is primarily a free trade agreement that allows goods and services to flow freely between India and Singapore.

sections.label: Free movement of persons
sections.summary: The language on free movement of persons allows such movement only for temporary purposes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There is language here on the free movement of persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But what it allows is the free movement of persons for temporary purposes.

sections.label: CECA Chapter 9 citizenship discretion
sections.summary: Chapter 9 of CECA does not change citizenship, permanent residence and long-term employment, so Singapore retains full discretion on admissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Chapter 9 of CECA does not change anything in relation to citizenship, permanent residence and long-term employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And this is very expressed in clause 9.2.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This means that Singapore retains full discretion on who it admits.

sections.label: Local employment by India investors
sections.summary: According to MTI, some 97,000 locals were employed in 2019 by organisations that invested in India.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: According to MTI, some 97,000 locals were employed in 2019 by organisations that invested in India.

sections.label: White Paper foreign worker limits
sections.summary: The White Paper expressly states that an unlimited number of foreign workers cannot be allowed in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I was actually in this House when the White Paper was being debated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And again, if you read the White Paper, it says very expressly, we cannot allow in an unlimited number of foreign workers.

sections.label: MOM work pass powers
sections.summary: MOM already has power to take away work passes for foreign workers from employers engaging in discriminatory practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Currently, MOM already has the power to take away work passes for foreign workers for employers who engage in discriminatory practices.

sections.label: Jobs and employment information release
sections.summary: The second amendment would proactively release information on Singaporeans' jobs and employment prospects, though much information already exists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The second amendment to proactively release information on jobs and employment prospects of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There is, actually, a great deal of information out there already.

sections.label: Free trade agreements information
sections.summary: The speaker says free trade agreement information is already public and on the MTI website, so the amendment is unnecessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In relation to free trade agreements, there are the agreements themselves out there in the public domain which anyone can read but I think very few do, except perhaps a few people like us lawyers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There is information on the MTI website that simplifies the benefits of free trade agreements for people and, of course, if more information is needed, if a debate is needed on the cost and benefits, we can always have Motions in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, in my view, I do not think the amendment is necessary because it insinuates that there is not enough information out there and we cannot make sensible decisions with the available information.

sections.label: Open foreign talent policy support
sections.summary: Trade associations and chambers almost unanimously agreed Singapore must maintain an open foreign talent policy and companies must implement fair workplace practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In dialogues which I had with trade associations and chambers (TACs) throughout the year, it is almost unanimous – I could say unanimous – that Singapore must maintain our open foreign talent policy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To quote Mr Farid Khan, President of Singapore Malay Chamber of Commerce, "Singapore must accept diversity and remain open and transparent in our foreign talent policy even as we scale up the number of graduates from Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) majoring in key disciplines where we have supply/demand gaps: information technology, cybersecurity, software engineering and the like." In the same breath, all agree that companies, both global MNCs and Singapore companies, need to implement fair practices in the workplace.

sections.label: Building information modelling professionals demand
sections.summary: BIM manager, project manager and architectural manager positions were filled by foreigners or outsourced because Singaporean architects and engineers lacked exposure to these technologies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Building information modelling (BIM) professionals were in high demand for their competences and skills early last year or in recent years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, positions, such as BIM managers, project managers and architectural managers, had to be filled by foreigners or outsourced to foreign companies because Singaporean architects and engineers were not sufficiently exposed to the convergence of these technologies with traditional engineering and architectural disciplines.

sections.label: Locals shunning certain jobs
sections.summary: Mr Ng shared that despite company commitment to training and job redesign, locals continue to shun physically strenuous, shift-work and remote-location jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Ng shared that while companies are committed to do all they can to transform their business model, redesign jobs, offer training and upskilling and reskilling opportunities to locals, there remains a near-to medium-term structural issue, that is, locals continue to shun certain jobs, for example, physically strenuous jobs, jobs that require shift work and workplaces in remote locations.

sections.label: Foreign manpower in food manufacturing
sections.summary: A considerable number of foreign manpower work in the food manufacturing sector, which exports about 60% of its manufacturing output overseas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, a considerable number of foreign manpower work in our food manufacturing sector that exports about 60% of its manufacturing output to overseas markets.

sections.label: Hiring Singaporeans for senior roles
sections.summary: Sixty-four percent of respondents hiring Singaporeans for senior roles find candidates lack relevant skills, and 53% report lack of work experience.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Sixty-four percent of respondents looking to hire Singaporeans for senior level roles – managers and above – are finding that candidates lack relevant skills and 53% of respondents report candidates lack necessary work experience.

sections.label: Declining fertility and working population
sections.summary: Singapore's Total Fertility Rate has declined for decades, hitting 1.1 in 2020, leading to a shrinking working population.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The future of that Singapore in that story will be sad one.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And as if this is not nightmarish enough, with Singapore's Total Fertility Rate (TFR) being in decline for a few decades and hitting a low of 1.1 in 2020, we will see the decline in the size of the Republic's working population.

sections.label: Foreign manpower in workforce
sections.summary: Foreign manpower makes up one-third of Singapore's total workforce and is present in many professions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Foreign manpower makes up one-third of our total workforce and are present in many professions.

sections.label: CECA claims and ministerial rebuttals
sections.summary: Some claim CECA caused an influx of Indian-origin workers harming Singaporean PMETs; Ministers Ong Ye Kung and Tan See Leng rebutted this on 6 July.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Some claim that CECA allowed for the influx of large numbers of workers of Indian origin, harming the interests of Singaporean PMETs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
