sentences.text: On 6 July, Ministers Ong Ye Kung and Tan See Leng gave thorough clarifications and rebuttals to such claims.

sections.label: Interlinked manpower strategies
sections.summary: Strategies are interlinked: attracting foreign investment, strengthening local companies, grooming the local workforce, and bringing in foreign manpower to complement locals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Our various strategies are interlinked: attracting foreign investment, strengthening local companies, grooming the local workforce through formal education and lifelong learning, and bringing in foreign manpower to complement the local workforce.

sections.label: Education, SkillsFuture and foreign PMET rules
sections.summary: Singapore updates education curricula, invests in SkillsFuture lifelong learning, and regulates foreign PMET entry through salary requirements, fair hiring guidelines and watchlists.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We develop a well-rounded and diversified education system, where curricula are regularly updated based on industry feedback, and which prioritises work attachments and internships, so that each graduating cohort is amply prepared for the workplace.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We also invest heavily in lifelong learning and implement a full suite of measures under SkillsFuture that encourages reskilling, so that Singaporeans can take on larger roles or enter new professions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The Government also regulates the entry of foreign PMETs and takes action against unfair treatment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: This includes imposing minimum age-salary requirements for EPs so that companies would recruit foreign PMETs of a certain quality who are more likely to complement local PMETs rather than compete directly with locals on wages; requiring companies to follow Tripartite Guidelines for Fair Employment Practices and fairly consider local jobseekers before recruiting foreigners; and paying special attention to companies with a concentration of foreign PMETs of a particular nationality.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: They may be placed on the Fair Consideration Framework Watchlist and have their EP privileges curtailed.

sections.label: COVID-19 and Singapore employment
sections.summary: The COVID-19 pandemic damaged the world economy, but local employment in Singapore rose by 14,900 in 2020 while overall employment shrank by 166,600.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 pandemic has caused incalculable damage to the world economy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: However, in 2020, local employment in Singapore increased by 14,900 even as overall employment shrank by 166,600.

sections.label: PMET unemployment rates
sections.summary: PMET unemployment has been kept low, but since 2015 the rate for PMETs aged 50 and above has trended above that for PMETs in general.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, we have managed to keep PMET unemployment low.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: However, since 2015, we have observed that the unemployment rate for PMETs aged 50 and above has been trending above that for PMETs in general.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package
sections.summary: A SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package was launched last year, with additional SkillsFuture Credit top-ups for those aged 40-60.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: A SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package was launched last year, and additional SkillsFuture Credit top-ups were made available for those aged 40-60.

sections.label: Subsidies for families and elderly
sections.summary: Preschool, school and higher learning subsidies reduce parents' burden, while Pioneer and Merdeka packages, MediShield Life and CareShield Life help with elderly parents' medical expenses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Increases in preschool subsidies, enhanced financial assistance schemes for schools, as well as subsidies and bursaries for Institutes of Higher Learning help to reduce the burden on parents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, the Pioneer Generation Package, Merdeka Generation Package, MediShield Life and CareShield Life help those who have to bear their elderly parents’ medical expenses.

sections.label: Legislating Tripartite Fair Employment Guidelines
sections.summary: The Government will legislate the Tripartite Fair Employment Guidelines and enhance its stand against unfair workplace practices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The Government is going to take a further step, of legislating the Tripartite Fair Employment Guidelines and enhancing our stand against unfair workplace practices.

sections.label: Singapore's IMD competitiveness ranking
sections.summary: Singapore slipped from No 1 to No 5 in IMD's latest world competitiveness rankings, ranking lower for factors including attitudes towards globalisation, skilled labour availability and immigration laws.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In the latest world competitiveness rankings by IMD, Singapore slipped from No 1 to No 5, because we ranked lower for factors, such as “attitudes towards globalisation”, “availability of skilled labour” and “immigration laws preventing companies from hiring foreign labour”.

sections.label: Foreign manpower curb risks
sections.summary: Calling for curbs on foreign manpower may win support but could become xenophobia and discourage companies from coming or staying.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Repeatedly calling for curbs on foreign manpower may win some support, but this could morph into xenophobia and discourage companies from coming here or remaining here.

sections.label: Indian EP holder share
sections.summary: Minister Tan See Leng said Indian nationals grew from one-seventh of EP holders in 2005 to one quarter in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Minister Tan See Leng has said that Indian nationals have grown from one-seventh of EP holders in 2005 to one quarter in 2020.

sections.label: Indian PMETs and CECA
sections.summary: The passage states the growing presence of Indian PMETs has nothing to do with CECA or special Government affinity for Indians.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In other words, even if CECA did not exist, our strategy of building a finance hub and ICT hub would mean that there would likely be as many Indian PMETs here.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: From 2005 to 2020, in the ICT sector, there were 35,000 jobs created for local PMETs, compared to a 25,000 increase in EP holders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In the finance sector, there were 85,000 jobs created for local PMETs, compared to a 20,000 increase in EP holders – four times as many.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: I have mentioned that India is a major exporter of skilled manpower in finance and ICT.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: IT students enrolled across various tertiary settings in Singapore were 7,600 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: According to an OECD report, India produced 585,000 ICT graduates in 2015, which also outnumber those in many other countries.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Some might even consider giving up on Singapore and going elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: It is clear that the growing presence of Indian PMETs in Singapore has nothing to do with CECA, nor any special affinity that the Government has for Indians.

sections.label: Same bar for Indian EPs
sections.summary: Indian EP holders must clear the same bar as other sources, with checks guarding against under-qualified EPs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Indian EP holders have to clear the same bar as those from other sources and checks are in place for all sources to guard against letting in under-qualified EPs.

sections.label: Careful naturalisation approvals
sections.summary: Naturalisation is handled more carefully, so many well-qualified Indian nationals wait long for PR/SC approvals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: When it comes to naturalisation, we are even more careful.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: This is why many well-qualified Indian nationals have yet to receive approvals for their PR/SC applications even after a long wait.

sections.label: Support for original Motion
sections.summary: The Government and PAP Members will support the original Motion and not the Workers' Party amendments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: I do not think the Workers’ Party needs to go along with them and add an unnecessary limb to the Motion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Hence, the Government and PAP Members will support the original Motion standing in Minister Lawrence Wong’s name and not the amendments proposed by the Workers’ Party.

sections.label: Sim Ann worried by exchange
sections.summary: Ms Sim Ann said the exchange between the speaker and the Minister for Manpower worried her because it seemed to be about whether some Singaporeans are local-born.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Just now, Ms Sim Ann mentioned that the exchange between me and the Minister for Manpower had worried her because we seemed to be talking about whether some Singaporeans are local-born or not.

sections.label: Doubts over DBS CEO nationality
sections.summary: Mr Leong Mun Wai has repeatedly cast doubt on DBS CEO Mr Piyush Gupta's nationality, and the speaker says someone must speak up for people like him.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Mr Leong Mun Wai from PSP has repeatedly cast doubt on the nationality of the CEO of DBS, Mr Piyush Gupta, and we have discussed this at length.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Here, I would like to say that somebody needs to speak up on behalf of people like Mr Piyush Gupta.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In fact, this type of argument is exactly what I referred to as drawing lines between Singaporeans.

sections.label: Singapore assets and headquarters
sections.summary: Singapore's assets under management stood at S$4.7 trillion in 2020, and more than 7,000 multinationals operate some form of headquarters there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Total assets under management in Singapore stood at S$4.7 trillion in 2020, having increased at around 15% to 17% compound annual growth rate over the previous five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In fact, the financial and fintech sectors created 2,500 jobs and are expected to create 6,500 more in 2021, particularly in technology, wealth management, corporate banking and insurance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Singapore is also a favoured location for multinational companies with more than 7,000 operating some form of headquarters in the city-state.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This is considerably more than Hong Kong with 1,389 regional headquarters, Sydney with 533, Tokyo with 531 and Shanghai with 470.

sections.label: Singaporeans working overseas
sections.summary: As of 2019, over 34,000 Singaporeans were living and working overseas, and possibly more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As of 2019, the population of Singaporeans living and working overseas stands at over 34,000 and may be even more.

sections.label: Working-age population and labour growth
sections.summary: The working-age population probably peaked in 2018 or 2019, and resident labour force growth will slow to 0.7% per annum over the next decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The working-age population has probably peaked already in 2018, 2019, and the resident labour force growth will slow to 0.7% per annum over the next decade, from 1.6% per annum, on average, between 2011 and 2016.

sections.label: Mid-career reskilling survey
sections.summary: A recent survey found 98% of respondents aged 56 to 65 believed in reskilling and upskilling, and the SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways programme has been extended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: According to a recent survey, 98% of respondents aged between 56 and 65 believed in reskilling and upskilling to stay relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways programme has been extended and enhanced to cater to demand.

sections.label: TeSA tech job placements
sections.summary: TeSA placed over 7,000 Singaporeans into tech jobs between April 2016 and September 2020, and more mid-career training is hoped for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Between April 2016 and September 2020, TeSA placed over 7,000 Singaporeans into tech jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I hope to see plans by the Government to increase the availability of such mid-career training and placement programmes for the tech sector, particularly for mid-career job seekers who are currently facing difficulties.

sections.label: Graduates during the pandemic
sections.summary: From April 2021, demand for SGUnited Traineeships eased as fresh graduates found other traineeships or full-time employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Another group that is understandably anxious would be the students who have just graduated or are graduating into the pandemic – the University, Polytechnic and ITE graduates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am glad to note that from April 2021, demand for SGUnited Traineeships or attachments has eased as fresh graduates found other traineeships or full-time employment opportunities.

sections.label: TAFEP fair employment practices law
sections.summary: TAFEP fair employment practices are enshrined in law, and TAFEP now has more powers to penalise workplace and employment discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Let us enhance our efforts to strengthen our Singaporean Core of workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I would first like to take this opportunity to convey my appreciation to the Government for making the significant decision of enshrining TAFEP fair employment practices into the law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Only when there is equal accessibility to employment opportunities can we then talk about creating good jobs for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Now that TAFEP has been given more powers to enforce penalties against workplace and employment discrimination, this will alleviate some of the anxieties experienced by our older workers and minorities.

sections.label: Foreign manpower and anti-discrimination laws
sections.summary: With tightened foreign manpower restrictions and new anti-discrimination laws, more Singaporeans should eventually find their anxieties easing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With the recent tightening of foreign manpower restrictions and newly enshrined anti-discrimination laws coming, I believe, gradually but surely, more Singaporeans should, eventually, find their anxieties easing.

sections.label: Singaporeans in senior bank roles
sections.summary: Singaporeans hold senior roles in foreign banks based on merit, and the Capability Transfer Programme could be enhanced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: All said, I must point out that there are Singaporeans who are holding senior roles in the foreign banks based on merit and it is not necessarily a situation where foreigners are the only ones dominating the senior positions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I, for one, know, and even if you do a quick search on Google and LinkedIn, it will show Singaporeans heading the business units or are in very senior positions in the Union Bank of Switzerland or UBS – I will not mention the names – even in Julius Baer, Deutsche Bank private banking, HSBC private banking and Pictet, and also Singaporeans holding front office positions, such as the Global Head of Treasury Markets at Standard Chartered Bank.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In addition, I would like to urge the Government to explore even the possibility of enhancing the Capability Transfer Programme.

sections.label: Population growth and PR numbers
sections.summary: Population growth over the last decade was the lowest since Independence, and the PR population size has been kept stable for years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Our population growth over the last decade has been the lowest since Independence and we have kept the size of our PR population stable for years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Many of our new citizens and PRs are spouses of Singaporeans and parents of Singaporean children.

sections.label: Support for Finance Minister Motion
sections.summary: The speaker cannot support Mr Leong Mun Wai's Motion but supports the Minister for Finance's Motion affirming Singapore stays open and connected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For those broad reasons and various reasons I have mentioned in my speech, I am not able to support the Motion in the name of Mr Leong Mun Wai.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I support the Motion in the name of the Minister for Finance, as it affirms that Singapore needs to stay open and connected to the world; it acknowledges the anxieties whilst, at the same time, laying out the existing calls for enhancements needed for policies to secure the livelihoods of Singaporeans in the long run.

sections.label: Rajaratnam's 1972 hinterland vision
sections.summary: In February 1972, then-Foreign Minister S Rajaratnam visualised embracing the world as Singapore's hinterland.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: As far back as in February 1972, our then-Foreign Minister S Rajaratnam visualised embracing the world as our hinterland.

sections.label: Rajaratnam Global City quote and ICT growth
sections.summary: The speaker quotes Rajaratnam on shaping the Global City wisely and boldly, and notes ICT grew over three-fold in two decades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: That vision, that wisdom, has helped to put us where we are today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: I quote the late Mr Rajaratnam in his speech saying: "But the Global City, now in its infancy, is the child of modern technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: It is the city that electronic communications, supersonic planes, giant tankers and modern economic and industrial organisation have made inevitable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Whether the Global City would be a happier place than the megalopolis out of whose crumbling ruins it is emerging will depend on how wisely and boldly we shape its direction and growth." Very true, words to remember: how we can be a happier place would depend on how wisely and boldly we shape its direction and growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Information and Communications Technology (ICT) sector has grown more than three-fold over the last two decades and employs well over 150,000 people.

sections.label: Infocomm job shortfalls and university places
sections.summary: Ministers cited unfilled infocomm jobs, future digital worker needs, and local university infocomm degree places rising from 800 to 3,100.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister for Manpower said in July that 6,000 jobs remained unfilled in the infocomm sector and there are not enough locals to fill the available jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In an interview last year, the Minister in charge of the Smart Nation Initiative said that the infocomm space will require 60,000 more professionals over the next three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: An Amazon Web Services (AWS) report earlier this year highlighted that Singapore would need an additional 1.2 million digital workers by 2025 to remain competitive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Replying to my Parliamentary Question on 26 July, the Minister for Education said that the number of places in information and digital technologies undergraduate degree courses in local Universities increased from 800 in 2010 to 3,100 last year.

sections.label: Secondary schools offering computing O level
sections.summary: Only 22 Secondary schools currently offer computing as an O level subject, available only from Secondary 3.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Currently, only 22 Secondary schools offer computing as an "O" level subject and this is available only from Secondary 3.

sections.label: Perfect A level scores of applicants
sections.summary: Both the 90th and 10th percentile of applicants offered places scored four As at A levels, essentially perfect scores.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Both the 90th and the 10th percentile of applicants offered places scored four As for their "A" levels – essentially, perfect scores.

sections.label: IHL CS intake Singaporeans
sections.summary: Institutes of Higher Learning should increase CS major intake and admit more Singaporeans with passion for technology who meet prerequisites.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Institutes of Higher Learning should move more quickly to increase their intake of CS majors and should admit more Singaporeans who can demonstrate a passion for technology and meet the prerequisite standards for the course.

sections.label: Government stamping out hiring discrimination
sections.summary: The Government must commit to stamping out discrimination in hiring and promotion, especially where competition for attractive jobs is keener.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government must commit to stamping out discrimination in the hiring and promotion process in companies, especially in firms where the competition for attractive and well-paying jobs is keener.

sections.label: Foreign managers hiring own kind
sections.summary: Some companies have ignored foreign managers hiring their own kind instead of the best qualified candidates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some companies have turned a blind eye to their foreign managers "hiring their own kind" instead of the best qualified candidates.

sections.label: Anti-discrimination legislation and reporting
sections.summary: Anti-discrimination legislation should let MOM prosecute discriminatory employers, with listed companies, MNCs and work pass applicants reporting workforce composition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Anti-discrimination legislation should provide the MOM powers to prosecute employers found engaging in discriminatory practices in hiring and promotions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To encourage companies to demonstrate their commitment to promoting more qualified women, minorities and Singaporeans in their senior leadership, listed companies in Singapore should be required to report the gender, racial and national composition of their boards as part of their ESG (environmental, social and governance) impact reporting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Foreign MNCs and startups which benefit from Government incentives and schemes should be made to submit yearly reports to MOM of the gender, race and nationality of employees at each level of their organisational hierarchy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Companies which apply for Employment Passes and S Passes should be required to submit to MOM a breakdown of employee numbers by nationality at each level of seniority within the company and in the department that the work pass applicant is being hired into.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: MOM should make transparent its criteria to determine what is an acceptable threshold for each industry and size of company.

sections.label: Singapore economy global technological diffusion
sections.summary: The Singapore economy can be characterised as linked to the global economy via technological diffusion, with job vacancies increasing as the labour force expanded.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As an organising framework, to think about the Motion before us, it is useful to characterise the Singapore economy as a country that is linked to the global economy via technological diffusion: a process that is facilitated by strong cross-border exchanges of goods, capital and people.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is a fact that even as the size of Singapore's labour force has expanded over the decades since Independence so that there are more people looking for jobs, the number of job vacancies to be filled has increased.

sections.label: FDI and job creation
sections.summary: As Singapore's labour force grew from under a million in 1978 to over three million in 2013, real FDI stock per worker rose more than ten times.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, the role of foreign direct investment in job creation.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I find it useful, in my own effort to understand the Singapore Story, to note that even as our total labour force increased by more than three times from less than a million in 1978 to over three million in 2013, the stock of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) per worker in real terms, adjusted for inflation, increased by more than 10 times.

sections.label: FDI stock growth versus foreign workforce
sections.summary: From 2013 to 2017, growth of the FDI stock far exceeded growth of Singapore's foreign workforce.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: You would find that the growth of the FDI stock just over this period, 2013 to 2017, again far exceeded the growth rate of the foreign workforce in Singapore.

sections.label: FDI stock in financial services
sections.summary: In 2017, more than 50% of total FDI stock went to financial and insurance services.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2017, more than 50% of the total FDI stock went to financial and insurance services, one of the industries in there.

sections.label: Large firms productivity and pay
sections.summary: Large firms, which many MNCs tend to be, are more productive and pay more for observationally identical workers.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Large firms, which many MNCs tend to be, are more productive and they pay more for observationally identical workers.

sections.label: Innovation driving productivity growth
sections.summary: Singapore must move from imitation to innovation, with productivity gains from innovative SMEs driving growth.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the next phase of Singapore’s economic development, it is not enough to rely on technologies developed abroad.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We must move from imitation to innovation just to maintain trend growth.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Much of the catch-up phase in the technological diffusion is probably nearly over.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, in the next stage, innovation will have to drive productivity growth.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A bigger share of the source of growth would have to come from productivity gains achieved by SMEs that are successful in their innovations.

sections.label: Labour force size and productivity
sections.summary: A large supply of entrepreneurs is needed for innovation, and a declining workforce slows productivity growth.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Given the high probability of failure in any innovative activity, having a large supply of workers who turn into entrepreneurs is necessary to ensure a sufficiently high aggregate rate of innovation that would need to drive the productivity growth, to allow us to attain trend growth as a mature economy.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Since it is people who create ideas, a declining workforce ultimately leads to slower productivity growth.

sentences.speaker: Prof Hoon Hian Teck (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It would appear then, just to maintain the trend growth, keeping the size of the labour force from declining is of paramount importance.

sections.label: Precarity and free trade
sections.summary: The speaker will argue against the claim that worker precarity has nothing to do with free trade or FTAs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In my contribution to this Motion, I will argue against the blanket claim that the precarity felt by our workers has absolutely nothing to do with free trade or, for that matter, FTAs.

sections.label: Free trade inequality and backlash
sections.summary: High-skilled and capital holders gain most from free trade, leaving the working class worse off and fuelling populist backlash, including against CECA.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Today, the major gainers in our nation’s stance on free trade are the high-skilled and those with access to capital.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These groups benefit disproportionately well from our open trading regime, leaving our less well-off working class – now, decidedly, the minority – in an even worse position.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It should, therefore, be of little surprise that, all over the world, we have witnessed populist challenges to globalisation: from the 1999 Seattle WTO protests, to the 2011 Occupy Wall Street movement, to the more recent Gilets Jaunes in France.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And, Mr Speaker, may I venture that the backlash against CECA also has its roots in the perceived inequality of the deal for our local workers.

sections.label: WSG and SkillsFuture adjustments
sections.summary: WSG and SkillsFuture are Singapore's adjustment programmes, though not solely for trade-related job displacement, with proposed refinements like redundancy insurance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Our equivalent adjustment programme is WSG and SkillsFuture, although these are not explicitly targeted at addressing trade-related job displacement alone.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I had previously spoken, during this year’s Committee of Supply debates, on potential refinements of our reskilling and reemployment programmes, including rolling out redundancy insurance, and making the Jobs Growth Incentive and Professional Conversion Programme permanent features of our policy landscape.

sections.label: India's output and population
sections.summary: India's output in a common currency is almost eight times larger than Singapore's, and even more so in population.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: India’s output, measured in a common currency, is almost eight times larger than ours; and, even more evidently, in terms of population.

sections.label: Wage effects of trade opening
sections.summary: Trade opening means minimum salary floors for foreign employment pass holders offer limited help, and local wages in exposed sectors may still face significant reductions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The upshot of trade opening is that minimum salary floors for foreign employment pass holders will only offer limited succour, and the growth of local wages for those in the same sector will still be reduced, so long as we begin from a relatively higher starting point.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Hence, even for Singaporeans who do not lose their jobs outright as a result of CECA, or any other FTA, there is still a chance that their salaries could face a significant hit, if they happen to work in sectors more exposed to trade liberalisation.

sections.label: Refining CECA third review
sections.summary: There is little reason not to seek to refine the deal, especially given the ongoing third review of the pact.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Still, there is little reason why we should not seek to refine the deal, especially in light of the ongoing third review of the pact.

sections.label: Winners' share and taxpayer burden
sections.summary: Unless trade winners contribute a share matching their boosted incomes, supporting displaced workers shifts the burden back to the Singaporean taxpayer.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While this is important, unless the winners from trade are definitively contributing a share consistent with their boosted incomes, this will end up shifting the burden of supporting displaced workers back to the Singaporean taxpayer.

sections.label: Tightening EP and S Pass criteria
sections.summary: The speaker says these elements need closer scrutiny and calls PM Lee's NDP Rally announcement on gradually tightening EP and S Pass criteria a heartening step.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In my view, these elements bear closer scrutiny and Prime Minister Lee’s announcement during this year’s NDP Rally that the Government will gradually tighten EP and S Pass criteria is a heartening step in this direction.

sections.label: Evaluating FTA benefits and costs
sections.summary: The speaker says clear-eyed evaluations of the benefits and costs of all FTAs, including CECA, are needed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even so, we need clear-eyed evaluations of the benefits and costs of all our FTAs, CECA included.

sections.label: Freedom of information on FTA data
sections.summary: The speaker calls for a freedom of information initiative releasing trade, production and labour market data on FTAs, and supports Pritam Singh's amended Motion.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: All such assertions should be based on evidence, obtained through careful analysis and deliberation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I call on this Government to institute a freedom of information initiative that will guarantee the full release of accurate and complete trade, production and labour market data, insofar as they pertain to the study of our FTAs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This should be at any level of disaggregation requested, albeit suitably anonymised, if necessary.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I should note that this is a routine practice in countries worldwide, from advanced economies like Australia, the European Union and the United States, to developing nations as diverse as Brazil, Moldova and Sri Lanka.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If we truly believe that FTAs have been good for our country, we have nothing to fear in releasing these data for further study and scrutiny.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I support the amended Motion advanced by the Leader of the Opposition Pritam Singh.

sections.label: Jobs and full employment
sections.summary: The Labour Movement believes jobs are the best welfare and full employment is the best protection for workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement believes that jobs are the best welfare and full employment is the best protection for our workers.

sections.label: Protecting mature PMEs
sections.summary: The speaker says mature PMEs aged 40 and above are more disadvantaged due to COVID-19, and there is a need to protect them against egregious companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Due to COVID-19 and its impact on businesses, we see that mature PMEs aged 40 and above are more disadvantaged due to their age and seniority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As much as we have debated and implemented policies and programmes to better support PMEs, there is still a need to protect our PMEs against egregious companies who exploit the system, treat workers unfairly.

sections.label: Insufficient local talent pool
sections.summary: The speaker states that mathematically the size of the local talent pool is insufficient to meet their needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mathematically, the size of our local talent pool is insufficient to meet their needs.

sections.label: Foreign talent complements local labour
sections.summary: Jobs that Singaporeans and foreign workers could have taken will be lost, so society must accept foreign talent and labour as complementary to local talent and labour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: All the jobs that could have been taken up by Singaporeans and foreign workers will be lost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, as a society, we need to embrace the concept that foreign talent and labour are complementary to our local talent and labour.

sections.label: New tribunal for workplace discrimination
sections.summary: At the National Day Rally, Prime Minister Lee announced a new tribunal for workplace discrimination and enhanced legislative powers for TAFEP in the Employment Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A few weeks ago, at the National Day Rally, Prime Minister Lee announced that there will be a new tribunal for workplace discrimination and the further enhancement of legislative powers for TAFEP in the Employment Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is such an important step to ensure fairness in the workplace when it comes to hiring – another key component in enhancing our workers' job security.

sections.label: Five-year commitment for newer schemes
sections.summary: It would be helpful if the Government explored committing to a five-year period for these newer schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: If the Government could explore the possibility of committing to a five-year period for these newer schemes, it would be helpful.

sections.label: Mandatory training hours and absentee payroll
sections.summary: The final proposal recommends mandatory training hours per year coupled with enhanced absentee payroll support to help employers and employees stay ahead of disruption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: My final proposal is to recommend mandatory training hours per year and to couple it with enhanced absentee payroll support to assist employers and employees with resources to continue to stay ahead of the disruption curve.

sections.label: Disagreement with Leong Mun Wai's Motion
sections.summary: The speaker calls it disingenuous for the PSP to focus on one or two components of a single FTA and does not support the Motion by Mr Leong Mun Wai.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It is, therefore, highly disingenuous for the PSP to simply focus on one or two components of a single FTA to create unnecessary anxieties, especially when it has been addressed in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, I completely disagree and am not in support of the Motion standing in the name of Mr Leong Mun Wai.

sections.label: MNCs and Chinese collaboration
sections.summary: Some MNCs include ExxonMobil, Katoen Natie and NEC, and work is ongoing with Chinese MNCs like Yonyou for collaboration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Some of the MNCs include ExxonMobil, Katoen Natie, NEC and we are currently working with some Chinese MNCs like Yonyou for collaboration.

sections.label: Tunity growth and training
sections.summary: Tunity has grown with employees, done national projects, built intellectual property, won a pharmaceutical MNC contract, and worked with IMDA on training mature PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In addition, Tunity has grown with their employees, done notable national projects, such as the National Gallery and National Heritage Board's inventory tracking systems, build intellectual property and, recently, secured another huge contract from another MNC in the pharmaceutical industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Moreover, they have worked closely with IMDA under the Company Led Training Programme to provide upskilling, training and employment to mature PMEs.

sections.label: Powers against workplace discrimination
sections.summary: Recent efforts to enhance powers to tackle workplace discrimination will further ease workers' minds on job security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Recent efforts to go further and enhance its powers to tackle workplace discrimination will go an even longer way in easing our workers’ minds on job security.

sections.label: Evolving systems for workforce competitiveness
sections.summary: Mitigating concerns by regularly evolving systems, structures and policies is the best way to create jobs, enhance wages and stay globally relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We should focus on how to mitigate these concerns by regularly evolving our systems, structures and policies to enable our workforce to compete confidently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This is the best way to create more jobs, enhance wages and ensure our continued relevance in the global community.

sections.label: CECA, FTAs and income inequality
sections.summary: The speaker did not call for refining CECA, cites a February 2020 CNA article on lowest household income inequality in almost 20 years, and notes post-tax Ginis improved while non-post-tax Ginis rose.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: I did not call explicitly for a refinement of CECA.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I would just like to also refer Assoc Prof Jamus Lim to an article that was published I think in CNA in February 2020, that the household income inequality at the end of 2019 was at its lowest in almost 20 years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We started the FTAs at the turn of this millennium.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And at the end of the period of the FTA signing, the Gini coefficient, after transfers, is lower.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, I think, just to put some perspective into what Assoc Prof Jamus Lim is talking about.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: I actually agree that our post-tax Ginis have improved in recent times, but that is, in fact, precisely because of something I pointed out, which is, that we have engaged in transfer policies to seek to ameliorate some of the implications of rising inequality.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: So, in fact, if you look at the non-post-tax Gini coefficients, they have, in fact, risen over time.

sections.label: Choice to be global hubs
sections.summary: The Government has explained many times that it is our choice to be a financial hub and a technology hub.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As the Government has explained many times, it is our choice to play this global game, to be a financial hub, to be a technology hub.

sections.label: PMET anxiety and retrenched residents
sections.summary: After a Robbie Fowler Liverpool reference, the passage says competition has increased for PMETs, MPs from both sides discussed Singaporeans' anxieties, and residents in their 40s and 50s were retrenched and still lack jobs despite CVs and reskilling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: And which Liverpool fan can forget when we welcomed God, or Robbie Fowler to the rest of you, back to heaven when Rafa brought him back from Annfield as a backup striker to Owen and Heskey.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: It has made things more competitive for our PMETs, and Members of Parliament from both sides of the House have talked about the anxieties felt by Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: I have spoken to residents, many in their 40s and 50s, who were retrenched and have yet to find a new job, despite sending out many CVs and making efforts to tap on various reskilling programmes.

sections.label: Fair hiring frameworks and TAFEP
sections.summary: The speaker says grievances are real, citing the Fair Consideration Framework and TAFEP, and welcomes measures to enshrine TAFEP in legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: I do not doubt that some of these grievances are real.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: That is the reason why we have the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) and Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP).

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: So, I was happy to hear of the commitment to ensuring that Singaporeans always get a fair chance, including measures to enshrine TAFEP in legislation in the Prime Minister's National Day Rally speech.

sections.label: Rejecting Leong Mun Wai's Motion
sections.summary: The speaker says it is dangerous to believe Singapore can lose this status, so the Motion in Mr Leong Mun Wai's name must be rejected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: It is dangerous to believe that it is okay to lose this status because we have many things to fall back on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: That is why I cannot accept and why I must reject the Motion standing in the name of Mr Leong Mun Wai.

sections.label: Hard to find skilled people
sections.summary: The speaker says rapid technology change means domain knowledge and technical skills are not readily available, and Singapore lacks enough people with these skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: Part of the reason it is so hard to find people is that technology is changing so rapidly and the depth of domain knowledge or specific technical skills is not yet readily available.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: We simply do not have enough Singaporeans with these skills.

sections.label: Longer Employment Pass approvals
sections.summary: The speaker's banking contacts say Employment Pass approvals now take months instead of days, even for senior jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: My banking contacts have shared that getting an EP now takes much longer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: EPs that used to get approved in days now take months, even for senior jobs.

sections.label: Bank hiring Singaporean graduates
sections.summary: At an MNC bank, the entry-level directive is to hire exclusively Singaporean fresh graduates and PMETs from professional conversion programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: At an MNC bank, at the entry level, the directive is now to hire exclusively Singaporean fresh graduates and PMETs who have gone through professional conversion programmes.

sections.label: Order for considering applicants
sections.summary: Hiring managers are asked to consider internal Singaporean applicants first, then internal EP holders, then external Singaporean hires, then external foreign hires.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: Hiring managers are also asked to consider internal Singaporean applicants first before internal EP holders, before external Singaporean hires and then only external foreign hires, in that order.

sections.label: Singaporeans living their dreams
sections.summary: The passage asks how Singaporeans can be denied the opportunity to live their dreams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: How can we deny these Singaporeans the opportunity to live their dreams?

sections.label: Tightening up and investing in Singaporeans
sections.summary: The passage says discrimination should be ferreted out, but the best rebalance is investing in Singaporeans until globally competitive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: So, yes, let us tighten up where we can, let us ferret out instances of discrimination because there is really no place for this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: But I say the best way to rebalance is to keep investing in Singaporeans until we are globally competitive.

sections.label: Mid-career reskilling programme job outcomes
sections.summary: In one mid-career reskilling programme, 40% of trainees landed a job within a couple of weeks of graduation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: In one of the mid-career reskilling programmes I am familiar with, 40% of the trainees landed a job within a couple of weeks of graduation.

sections.label: Young graduates' skills on CVs
sections.summary: A startup CEO says few young Singaporean graduates have these skills on their CVs, while many in India and Jakarta do through boot camps and short courses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: According to the CEO of a startup which uses big data to understand skills, few young Singaporean graduates have these on their CVs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: Interestingly enough, many young graduates in India and Jakarta do, not through their university courses but through boot camps and external short courses they attend.

sections.label: Empowering Singaporeans to reskill
sections.summary: The passage calls for giving Singaporeans tools to assess skills, curating courses with industry, and more granular job skills data for MOM.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: We can do more – the Government and employers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: We need to empower Singaporeans to take ownership of their own reskilling and career development by, first, giving them the tools to understand where their skills stand versus their peers, where their skills, or lack thereof, are at risk, and then what they can do to start their reskilling journey or nudge them on the jobs they can put their hands up for.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: Tertiary institutions can work with industry to curate these courses and boot camps and guide their students on which ones to take for the jobs they want.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: Know the skills, get the skills, send in the applications showing the skills, and MOM will make sure that companies cannot ignore you.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: To do this, much more granularity is needed on the skills required for each job.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: This granularity will also allow MOM to be more circumspect and discerning when employers come claiming that they cannot find any Singaporeans with the skills and to ensure that reskilling programmes supported by public funds will have a better track record of outplacement.

sections.label: Supporting the Motion amid change
sections.summary: The passage supports the Motion and notes COVID-19 has accelerated change, with jobs transformed, created and becoming obsolete.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my suggestions in this speech, I support the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Thereafter, I will put the question in respect of each Motion to the House for voting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We all know that change is the only constant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: COVID-19 has accelerated change further with digital transformation, new business models and new ways of working.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In the coming years, we will see more disruptions and volatility in the global economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As entire industries adapt to these changes, many jobs will be transformed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: New jobs will be created but some jobs will become obsolete.

sections.label: Government approach to openness
sections.summary: The Government's approach is to keep Singapore open and connected to the world as the only way to secure its future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I have set out in my opening speech the Government's approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We keep Singapore open and connected to the world because that is the best, indeed, the only way to secure our future.

sections.label: Open economy downsides and adjustments
sections.summary: An India shock may follow Indian liberalisation under WTO, and Singapore manages downsides through work pass flows, fair employment and helping displaced workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: CECA or not, if India liberalises and opens up, just based on WTO, there will be an India shock, which we will have to deal with and adjust to as we had to do when China joined the WTO.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There are downsides to being an open economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That is why we work very hard to deal with these downsides by managing the flow of foreign work pass holders, upholding fair employment at workplaces and helping every displaced worker to get back into jobs.

sections.label: Openness and racial politics risks
sections.summary: Staying open is existential for a small city-state, and racial or xenophobic undertones in politics would lead down a slippery slope.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: First, as a small city-state, staying open is not just essential; it is existential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Second, if we start having racial or xenophobic undertones in our politics, we will be going down a very slippery slope.

sections.label: Job challenges not from FTAs
sections.summary: Public data shows job challenges do not arise from FTAs, let alone CECA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Dr Tan See Leng had given a whole range of data just now and, as I have said, there is more than enough public data out there to show that the job challenges we face do not arise from FTAs, let alone CECA.

sections.label: Population, immigration and foreign manpower proposals
sections.summary: Population growth was the lowest since Independence, immigration keeps ethnic balance stable, and Leong Mun Wai's three foreign manpower adjustments are unrelated to CECA and FTAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In any case, the evidence is clear: population growth over the last decade has been the lowest since our Independence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, there should be no doubt that we have already been very tight at the overall level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have also emphasised that our immigration policies will continue to ensure that the ethnic balance remains stable for our citizen population.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As far as foreign manpower policy is concerned, after all the fire and brimstone from Mr Leong Mun Wai, all that he has asked for are three adjustments to our policies: raising EPs and S Pass qualifying salaries, imposing a levy on EPs and imposing a cap of 10% per nationality in any company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: These proposals have nothing to do with CECA and FTAs.

sections.label: Government view on data transparency
sections.summary: The Government sees data and transparency as means to better governance, and data is not always an unmitigated good.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I would say, the Government has a different view.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We see data and transparency as a means to better governance and it is not always the case that data is necessarily an unmitigated good.

sections.label: Data release and foreign workers
sections.summary: The Government rejects the Workers' Party's amendments, citing risks of exposing dependence on foreign workers and hostile actors disrupting labour flows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Where it is possible, we have released those data, but is it such a good thing to let the whole world know our dependence on foreign workers and from which particular country?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I think it was one of the Workers' Party Members who also said that one has to be careful about hostile actors that may exploit our social fault lines to disrupt our society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, should we not be careful about external parties that may hold us to ransom by threatening to disrupt or terminate our labour flows, especially in certain key Industries?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We should, therefore, think through carefully these broader considerations when we talk about data release and information policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This is why the Government cannot accept the Workers' Party's amendments to this Motion.

sections.label: Rejecting racial undertones in politics
sections.summary: The speaker hopes it is confirmed that negative racial undertones in political debates must not take root and that the Workers' Party will reject the PSP's Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In that spirit, I hope he will confirm that we cannot give credence to negative racial undertones in our political debates, that we must never allow such politics to take root in this House and in Singapore, and that the Workers' Party will reject the PSP's Motion.

sections.label: Government data provision policy
sections.summary: The Government will provide data when asked and when in the national interest, consulting widely with stakeholders including tripartite partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The Government will provide data when it is asked for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Where we think it is in the national interest to provide such data, we will certainly do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will consult widely with our stakeholders, especially with our tripartite partners.

sections.label: Building fairer inclusive society
sections.summary: The priority is to build a fairer, more equal and more inclusive society after the crisis, entering an uncertain post-pandemic world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Our priority is to build a fairer, more equal and more inclusive society as we emerge from this crisis and enter a more uncertain and volatile post-pandemic world.

sections.label: Stance against racism and xenophobia
sections.summary: The speaker asks Members to take a firm stance against racism and xenophobia by voting for the Motion and rejecting the PSP's Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we have to decide where we stand and make a choice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I say, we take a firm and unequivocal stance against racism and xenophobia and, so, I ask all Members in this House to vote for the Motion standing in my name and to reject the PSP's Motion.

sections.label: Responding to CECA debate challenge
sections.summary: The speaker has 40 minutes to respond in the House to Minister K Shanmugam's challenge to debate on CECA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, I only have 40 minutes for my speech.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: I come to this House to respond to a challenge by Minister K Shanmugam to debate on CECA.

sections.label: Foreign professionals under EP SP schemes
sections.summary: It states that foreign professionals brought in under EP and SP schemes lack quotas and displace the local workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The provisions on people movement in FTAs like CECA are only a small part of a much larger problem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: But those that are brought in and masked under the EP and SP schemes are not, by definition, really foreign talent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: They are foreign professionals let in without quota, resulting in displacement of our own workforce.

sections.label: PME jobs and PRs awarded
sections.summary: It states 380,000 PME jobs were created for locals from 2005 to 2020 while 600,000 PRs went to work pass holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Three hundred and eighty thousand PME jobs created for locals, and that is for both Singaporeans and PRs, from 2005 to 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: But during the same period, 600,000 PRs had been awarded to work pass holders.

sections.label: Quota to scale down foreign workers
sections.summary: It proposes giving employers a quota now in exchange for a promise to scale down foreign workers in three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: At some point, we have to change and this is a golden opportunity because now we can tell the employers work harder, "We can give you the quota now, but make sure you promise to scale down your people in three years' time." This is the opportunity to convince the employers to work together and we change the course of our economy.

sections.label: Foreign talent policy and capability building
sections.summary: It states the foreign talent policy contributes little to capability building partly because the Singaporean Core is affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The whole foreign talent policy, as far as we can see up to now, contributes little to our capability building, partly because our Singaporean Core are being affected.

sections.label: GLC manager on foreigner dependence
sections.summary: It recounts a GLC senior manager saying overhauling his foreigner-dependent system would be costly, but change is still needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Like a GLC senior manager, who is a very close friend, recently shared with me, "Ah, if you want me to overhaul my whole system now, it will be very high cost because it's totally dependent on foreigners now." But I think we still have to make the change.

sections.label: PSP position on foreign talent
sections.summary: It reiterates PSP's five positions, including that foreign talent policy causes displacement and CECA is not net beneficial.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat mentioned about my PR recommendation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: I recommend to control the number, manage the number down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: I actually said the recommendation is for work pass holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, I am in support of Singaporeans with foreign spouses and giving the PR to the foreign spouses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: But for this recommendation, I am referring to PR and citizenship to the work pass holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, to reiterate PSP's position: one, we think the foreign talent is not a silver bullet to solve all our problems; two, the foreign talent policy is the root cause of the influx of foreigners and that has caused a significant number of displacement of Singaporeans; three, unfair wage competition is the main economic driver of the displacement; four, decisive and concrete measures are now needed to rebalance our job market; five, and lastly, the FTAs and CECA are part of the equation when we consider immigration and employment policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: And unless the Government can provide new information to prove otherwise, unfortunately, as of today, we still cannot agree that CECA is net beneficial to Singapore.

sections.label: Wage disadvantage against Singaporeans
sections.summary: Speaker says the wage disadvantage against Singaporeans must be eliminated, citing the 17% employer's CPF contribution as a direct differential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Okay, in terms of the policy: firstly, I think you really need to eliminate the wage disadvantage against Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: I do not think Minister Tan See Leng's two attempts to reply to my EP levy as a necessity to equalise the compensation package of the EPs and Singaporeans really answered the question, because the 17% employer's CPF contribution is a direct differential.

sections.label: Freedom of Information Act call
sections.summary: The passage urges the Government to introduce a Freedom of Information Act soon so Singaporeans can make informed opinions and judgements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Singaporeans have the right to information in order to make informed opinions and judgement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: We urge the Government to introduce the Freedom of Information Act as soon as possible, although we are not the first one to raise this.

sections.label: Standing parliamentary select committees
sections.summary: It recommends setting up a standing parliamentary select committee in every Ministry with ruling and alternative party representatives to improve information flow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: To this end, we recommend the setting up of a standing parliamentary select committee in every Ministry, with representatives from both the ruling and alternative parties to improve information flow to facilitate more substantial policy deliberation.

sections.label: Hard work and policy direction
sections.summary: It says NTUC leaders work hard, but the overall policy direction yields lowly-paid workers needing support, vulnerable PMETs and underemployment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: I believe Mr Patrick Tay and all the NTUC leadership and the NTUC staff are working very hard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: But if the overall policy is pointing at a different direction, the results that come out of their hard work speak for itself: lowly-paid workers constantly needing governmental financial support to get by despite working full-time; PMETs in their 40s and 50s finding themselves extremely vulnerable to discrimination; and now, underemployment.

sections.label: Foreign talent policy effects
sections.summary: It states the foreign talent policy, contrary to Population White Paper promises, created an imbalanced population, diluted national identity, inadequate innovation and worker displacement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Hon Members of this House, contrary to the original promises presented in the Population White Paper, the foreign talent policy has created in Singapore an imbalanced population with a diluted national identity, an economy with inadequate technological innovation and significant displacement of Singaporean workers.

sections.label: Fair policies with Singaporean interest first
sections.summary: It calls for policies designed and executed fairly with Singaporean interest first, and urgent concrete steps with suggestions to alleviate the problem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: We want these policies to be designed and executed fairly, with Singaporean interest first.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: We call for urgent and concrete steps to be taken to alleviate the current problem and we have given suggestions on what needs to be done.

sections.label: Philip Wen driving Grab
sections.summary: Mr Philip Wen, a former bank senior vice president, now drives Grab for a living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Many of us have heard or read about the story of Mr Philip Wen, whom I happen to know.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: He was a senior vice president of a bank but now has to drive Grab for a living.

sections.label: PMET survey sad stories
sections.summary: Many more sad stories were found through a survey of 750 PMET respondents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Yet, they are forced into a no-win situation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: There are many more sad stories, as we discovered through our survey of 750 PMET respondents.

sections.label: Singapore openness to foreign talent
sections.summary: Members including Prof Hoon Hian Teck and Minister Lawrence Wong said Singapore must stay open and welcome foreign talent to thrive.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment and Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: For the last eight hours or so, this is exactly what many of the Members of this House, including Prof Hoon Hian Teck and Minister Lawrence Wong, have said: that Singapore has to continue to remain open and have to welcome some of these foreign talent if we want to continue to thrive and grow.

sections.label: Leong Mun Wai CECA clarification
sections.summary: The speaker clarifies Mr Leong Mun Wai's point on CECA, noting Minister Ong Ye Kung cited PSP leaders' references to CECA.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Mr Leong Mun Wai asked me a question or suggested something, so I thought I should clarify through yourself, Mr Speaker, Sir.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He said: "Prior to my post on 21 June 2021, I have not mentioned CECA and I asked the Minister Shanmugam and he did not say anything." I am not quite sure what the purport or the point Mr Leong makes, because Minister Ong Ye Kung had said during the July debate, gave chapter and verse for the various times when PSP leaders had referred to CECA.

sections.label: Motion on Government policies
sections.summary: The Motion states the Government will update and improve policies, while objecting to policies said to lead to ruin.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: My Motion specifically states that the Government will continue to update and improve our policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: What we object to are muddle-headed policies that will lead us to the path of ruin and what Mr Leong suggested, what the PSP suggested, in our opinion, will get us there.

sections.label: WP voting on Motions
sections.summary: The WP will vote accordingly on both Motions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: On both Motions, the WP will vote accordingly.

sections.label: NTUC role in tripartism
sections.summary: The speaker cites 1985 CPF cuts and the 2008 crisis to argue NTUC is not the weak link in tripartism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: As he was in the 1980s, building a derivatives platform in Tokyo, was he aware that in the 1985 recession, NTUC and the unions, together with the Government, worked with workers to take a 15% cut in CPF to help Singapore go through a difficult time?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: And during the 2008 Global Financial Crisis, under the leadership of then Secretary-General, Mr Lim Swee Say, to upturn the downturn?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: So, I do not think NTUC is the weak link in tripartism.

sections.label: NTUC welfare and wage policy
sections.summary: The speaker says NTUC has done a tremendous job on general worker welfare but sees room for improvement in wage policy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: When it comes to talking about general welfare for workers and all that, I think NTUC has done a tremendous job as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: But when it comes to wage policy, I think there is some room for improvement.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model and National Wages Council
sections.summary: The speaker says the Progressive Wage Model aims at sustainable good wages and that NTUC and the Labour Movement are important to the National Wages Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: I think this is something that we always strive to do our best.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: We do not want to overstate the work that we have done for the Progressive Wage Model, but it is precisely a way that we can implement good wages for workers by making sure that it is sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: The second thing that we must note is that NTUC and the Labour Movement have been an important part of the National Wages Council.

sections.label: Collective agreements and Worker 4.0
sections.summary: The speaker says unions benchmark workers by work type when renewing collective agreements, and NTUC's Worker 4.0 covers wages, welfare and work prospect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
sentences.text: Every union, through the branches that they represent, every time when we renew a collective agreement, we make sure the workers are benchmarked to the type of work that they do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
sentences.text: As we know, recently, when NTUC launched Worker 4.0, we talked about the three Ws: wages, welfare and work prospect.

sections.label: NTUC FairPrice and cost of living
sections.summary: The speaker says NTUC FairPrice is about mitigating the cost of living compared to other merchants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad
sentences.text: When we talk about NTUC FairPrice, we are talking about mitigating the cost of living compared to other merchants.

sections.label: AmCham survey data
sections.summary: The speaker says the data cited came from a survey of American companies, a preview shared by the American Chamber of Commerce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: So, I cannot help but have to stand up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: He mentioned the data that I shared in my speech that came from the survey of American companies, a preview of the survey that the American Chamber of Commerce (AmCham) shared with me.

sections.label: Singaporean PMETs speaking up for jobs
sections.summary: The passage states that Singaporean PMETs who do not speak up or show hunger for jobs will lose them to those who do.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang
sentences.text: If, as Singaporean PMETs, we do not speak up, we do not ask for the job, we do not show hunger for our jobs, then, of course, those who speak louder, those who are more enthusiastic, those who appear more hungry, will get the job.

sections.label: Pritam Singh's amendments to Motion
sections.summary: The passage describes Pritam Singh's two amendments: replacing "supports" with "calls for stronger" and inserting a new limb (f) on releasing jobs and FTA information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Pritam Singh's amendment number 1 is in part (c) of Minister Wong's Motion to delete the word "supports" at the start of the sentence and to replace it with "calls for stronger".

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Pritam Singh's amendment number 2 is to insert a new limb (f), which reads, "calls on the Government to proactively release information on jobs and employment prospects of Singaporeans and the costs and benefits of Free Trade Agreements and foreign worker policies, with a view to formulating better policies to ensure Singaporeans secure good jobs in Singapore and are not disadvantaged when seeking employment".

sections.label: Motion part (c) and amendment outcome
sections.summary: The passage states part (c) remains original, the new limb (f) amendment falls, Workers' Party MPs' dissent is recorded, and Leong Mun Wai's Motion is next.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Part (c) of the original Motion remains in its original form.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The amendment to have a new limb (f) falls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Can the Workers' Party Members of Parliament have their dissent recorded, please?

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We will now deal with Mr Leong Mun Wai's Motion on Foreign Talent Policy.
